A YOUTH ENSEMBLE DOCUMENTARY SERIES

TEN YEARS
LATER

Five friends. Three cities. One decade between who they imagined they would become and who they are now.

LOGLINE

AN INDEPENDENT FEATURE DOCUMENTARY ABOUT A GENERATION COMING OF AGE.

Ten years ago, the director filmed five international students imagining their futures. A decade later, the camera returns to them across Shanghai, Berlin, and Silicon Valley.

Four have built lives beyond the traditional workplace - through music, stand-up, cinematography, and art. One followed a more conventional path into technology.

The film observes how a generation shapes itself amid globalization, shifting careers, and the age of AI. Did we become who we thought we would be? What steers a life: choice, talent, courage, or fate?

SYNOPSIS

FROM THE LIVES WE IMAGINED TO THE LIVES WE BUILT.

Ten Years Later began with footage the director made of her college friends. They studied seemingly “proper” subjects - mathematics, pre-med, international relations, and economics - while pouring themselves into music, moving images, performance, and art.

A decade later, four have turned those interests into careers. Feezy is an influential Chinese rapper and producer. Zigga moves between rap, stand-up, and social media. Wei photographs global brands while pursuing art and experimental music in Germany. Dawei left pre-med for cinematography and is reconsidering the path after a serious on-set accident.

Violet took the more conventional route: consulting, a return to school for computer science, and now software engineering in Silicon Valley - directly exposed to the disruption of AI.

Moving between archival youth footage and present-day life, the film follows five people in different cities and professions, all living through the same historical moment.

FEATURED SUBJECTS

FIVE LIVES.
ONE CIRCLE OF FRIENDSHIP.

Feezy

Rapper / Producer

A prominent voice in Chinese hip-hop, active both in music production and mainstream television.

Zigga

Rapper / Creator

A rap collective member, food creator, and stand-up comedian who has built a life around expression.

Wei

Photographer / Artist

A commercial photographer for international brands, an art photographer, and a graduate student in experimental music in Germany.

Dawei

Cinematographer

He left pre-med to shoot music videos for artists and bands. After a serious production accident, he is considering a new direction.

Violet

Software Engineer

After consulting and graduate school in computer science, she joined a North American tech company and now works on the front line of AI disruption.

A community of friendship: they witness one another, reflect one another, and face the changing times together.

STILLS

THEME & KEYWORDS

GROWING UP.
FINDING A SELF.
FIGURING IT OUT.

YOUTH & GROWTH / SELF-DISCOVERY / ENSEMBLE / A COMMUNITY OF FRIENDSHIP

The film offers a kind of reassurance: in a world changing faster and offering fewer standard answers, no one has to force themselves into a single template of success.

The world is large enough. Every field is large enough. Each person can find a place within it, and figure out a life one step at a time.

OUTLOOK

A FILM THAT RETURNS
EVERY TEN YEARS.

We hope to develop the film into a long-term documentary project - returning to the same group of people once every decade.

The years from twenty to thirty are long enough to test choices and perseverance, yet within the arc of a life they are only a beginning: the start of learning how to live with oneself and stand firmly in the world.

Each return will continue to observe how they evolve with their time, build relationships, and reorder their lives and values.

We want to preserve this slow process of “figuring it out” - not to judge different lives, but to gently affirm, decade after decade, that everyone can find a place in the world.

CREW

JIAYING HE
DIRECTOR

A venture capital investor working close to cycles of entrepreneurship and technology, Jiaying has long observed how industries rise and fall, how society changes, and how individual lives are carried through those shifts.

Before venture capital, she worked in advertising and technology, ran her own advertising studio, and directed commercial films.

She served as executive director of the documentary Pearls of the Earth, winner of Best Feature Documentary at the Barcelona Planet Film Festival and Best Documentary Editing at the Paris World Cinema Awards, with four nominations at the Rome International Film Festival.
